headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Moralis documentation spans 978 pages with 100% crawl coverage and zero broken links. API reference coverage is weak at 28.06% despite 884 API pages detected, leaving 71.94% of API surface undocumented or poorly linked to usage examples. Example code reliability shows 0% detection across all pages, flagged as a likely JS-rendering detection limitation requiring manual validation. Freshness metadata appears on only 4.81% of pages (47 pages), creating significant staleness risk (79.21%) that undermines user trust and AI retrieval quality. SEO/geo issues affect 22.26% of pages (218 pages), reducing discoverability.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Code examples fail or are non-runnable
key_findings.business_consequence: Run smoke + expected-output checks and auto-fix broken snippets.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

priority_actions.title: Add last-updated timestamps to all 978 pages via automated frontmatter injection or CMS workflow
priority_actions.why_this_first: Fixes 79.21% stale risk and 4.81% freshness coverage in one pass, immediately boosting user trust and AI retrieval confidence across entire site.

priority_actions.title: Audit and document the 636 API pages (71.94% of 884) missing usage examples or reference links, prioritizing top 50 by traffic
priority_actions.why_this_first: Directly unblocks developer onboarding and reduces support volume by connecting API surface to practical usage patterns for most-visited endpoints.

priority_actions.title: Restructure content on low-chunkability pages (17.28% pass rate) by adding subheadings, breaking long paragraphs, and splitting monolithic guides
priority_actions.why_this_first: Improves vector search and LLM context quality for 810+ pages, directly lifting retrieval readiness from 54.37 weak band toward usable AI support.

strengths: Zero broken internal, docs, or repository links across 978 pages with 95% link verification confidence
100% crawl coverage with 979 discovered pages and effective trap URL filtering (46 skipped)
Strong citationability at 100% and answerability at 99.9% for AI retrieval use cases
risks: 71.94% of 884 detected API pages lack adequate usage documentation or reference coverage, blocking developer onboarding
0% example reliability detection across 978 pages suggests JS-rendered code blocks invisible to crawlers, preventing validation of runnable samples
79.21% stale risk due to only 4.81% freshness metadata coverage (47 pages), eroding trust and AI answer accuracy
22.26% SEO/geo issue rate (218 pages) limits organic search visibility and regional discoverability
limitations: External audit cannot verify actual code example correctness, runtime behavior, or dependency versioning; 0% detection likely reflects JS-rendered samples invisible to crawler, not true absence.
API coverage metric (28.06%) measures doc-to-API linking and reference completeness but cannot assess whether documented endpoints match current production API contract or SDK versions.
Staleness risk (79.21%) is inferred from missing last-updated metadata; pages without timestamps may still be current, and pages with timestamps may contain outdated technical details.
automation_first: Deploy CI/CD hook to inject last-updated Git commit dates into frontmatter for all 978 pages, eliminating 95.19% freshness gap and cutting stale risk from 79.21% to near zero with zero ongoing manual effort.
Implement nightly link checker with Slack alerts to maintain zero broken links as site scales beyond 978 pages, preserving 95% link confidence and preventing future user frustration or SEO penalties.

Build automated chunkability linter (heading density, paragraph length, list usage) to flag pages below 17.28% threshold during PR review, preventing new low-quality content and guiding writers toward LLM-friendly structure before merge.
